content.text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring carrying three substituents:
- At the right-hand vertex, a vinyl chain: CH=CH–COOH.
- At the upper-left vertex, an NO2 group.
- At the lower-left vertex, a Cl.

Ring positions: the vinyl-bearing carbon is C1 (right, at about 345,210). Going up-left, C2 is at (260,160) and is a plain CH. C3 at (180,210) carries the NO2. C4 at (180,300) carries the Cl. C5 at (260,345) is a CH, and C6 at (345,300) is a CH. So the compound is 3-nitro-4-chlorocinnamic acid, 4-chloro-3-nitrophenyl.

The double bond is drawn with the ring side up-left and the COOH side down-right. The ring is at (345,210), the first alkene carbon at (425,160), the second at (505,210), and the carbonyl carbon at (585,160). The ring carbon and the carbonyl carbon sit on opposite sides of the double bond, so the geometry is trans (E).

SMILES: OC(=O)/C=C/c1ccc(Cl)c([N+](=O)[O-])c1
